symptom: PC1 statically configured with IP 192.168.10.10/24, gateway 192.168.10.1. Cannot ping gateway or Server1 in VLAN 10. Cable and link light are fine.
topology_note: SW1 access port Fa0/5 (PC1) should be in VLAN 10; SW1 SVI VLAN10 = 192.168.10.1; Server1 on Fa0/6, VLAN 10.
show_outputs:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN10 SALES: Fa0/6
VLAN20 GUEST: Fa0/5
---
SW1# show interfaces fa0/5 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (GUEST)
expected_fault: Access port Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10, isolating PC1 from its gateway and same-VLAN server.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 30 on SW2 cannot reach PCs or the gateway in VLAN 30 on SW1 across the inter-switch trunk, though VLAN 30 works fine locally on each switch.
topology_note: SW1 Gi0/1 trunk to SW2 Gi0/1 should carry VLANs 10,20,30,40. Gateway SVI VLAN30 resides on SW1.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port: Gi0/1  Mode: trunk
Vlans allowed on trunk: 1-29,31-4094
Vlans allowed and active in management domain: 1-29,31-40
expected_fault: VLAN 30 has been pruned from the trunk's allowed VLAN list on Gi0/1, so VLAN 30 traffic cannot cross the trunk between switches.

symptom: Users report intermittent connectivity and switch logs show recurring 'native VLAN mismatch' messages between SW1 and SW2.
topology_note: Trunk link SW1 Gi0/2 - SW2 Gi0/2; native VLAN should match (VLAN 1) on both ends.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces gi0/2 trunk
Native vlan: 1
---
SW2# show interfaces gi0/2 trunk
Native vlan: 99
---
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/2
expected_fault: Native VLAN is set to VLAN 1 on SW1 but VLAN 99 on SW2, causing untagged traffic to land in the wrong VLAN.

symptom: After connecting new switch SW3, VLANs configured on SW3 cannot communicate with corresponding VLANs on SW1; only default VLAN traffic passes.
topology_note: Link SW1 Fa0/24 to SW3 Fa0/24 is intended to be an 802.1Q trunk carrying VLANs 10,20,30.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces fa0/24 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Fa0/24 on SW1 is configured as an access port instead of a trunk, so only the default VLAN passes between switches.

symptom: PC5 (192.168.20.15/24) can ping other hosts on its own subnet but cannot ping anything outside VLAN 20, including 8.8.8.8.
topology_note: Router R1 sub-interface Gi0/0.20 = 192.168.20.1/24 is the correct gateway for VLAN 20.
show_outputs:
PC5> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.20.15
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.20.100
---
PC5> ping 192.168.20.1
Request timed out.
expected_fault: PC5 is configured with default gateway 192.168.20.100, which does not exist on the subnet, instead of the correct router address 192.168.20.1.

symptom: All PCs in VLAN 10 lost connectivity to the gateway and to every other subnet at the same time.
topology_note: Router R1 Gi0/0 = 192.168.10.1/24 serves as the VLAN 10 gateway.
show_outputs: R1# show ip interface brief\nGigabitEthernet0/0  192.168.10.1  YES manual administratively down  down
expected_fault: Gateway interface Gi0/0 on R1 is administratively shut down, so no VLAN 10 host can reach the gateway.

symptom: Newly deployed PCs in the finance VLAN cannot ping their configured default gateway, even though cabling and switch ports test fine.
topology_note: Finance VLAN 40 hosts are addressed 192.168.40.0/24; router sub-interface for VLAN 40 was just provisioned.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config interface gi0/0.40
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.40
 encapsulation dot1Q 40
 ip address 192.168.4.1 255.255.255.0
---
PC> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.40.20
Default Gateway: 192.168.40.1
expected_fault: Router sub-interface Gi0/0.40 is addressed on the wrong subnet (192.168.4.1/24) instead of 192.168.40.1/24, so it does not share a subnet with the VLAN 40 hosts.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 50 cannot ping their gateway 192.168.50.1, but PCs in every other VLAN on the same switch reach their gateways normally.
topology_note: Multilayer switch SW1 has SVI interface VLAN50 configured as the gateway for VLAN 50.
show_outputs:
SW1# show ip interface brief
Vlan50   192.168.50.1   YES manual up   down
---
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN50 HR: (no ports assigned)
expected_fault: VLAN 50 SVI line protocol is down because no switch port is currently assigned to VLAN 50, so the gateway interface stays unreachable.
concept_tag: SVI Down - No Active VLAN Ports

symptom: Several new PCs in VLAN 10 receive an IP address of 169.254.x.x and cannot reach any network resource.
topology_note: DHCP server on R1 serves pool DHCP-VLAN10 for 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip dhcp pool DHCP-VLAN10
Total addresses: 50
Leased addresses: 50
---
R1# show ip dhcp conflict
(none)
expected_fault: DHCP pool DHCP-VLAN10 is fully leased (50/50 addresses used), so new clients get no offer and self-assign an APIPA address.

symptom: PCs in the remote VLAN 60 (accounting) never receive a DHCP-assigned IP address, while PCs in VLAN 10 on the same router work fine.
topology_note: DHCP server is a dedicated host at 192.168.10.50 in VLAN 10; VLAN 60 is a separate subnet reachable only through router R1.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config interface gi0/0.60
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.60
 encapsulation dot1Q 60
 ip address 192.168.60.1 255.255.255.0
(no ip helper-address configured)
expected_fault: The VLAN 60 sub-interface has no ip helper-address pointing to the DHCP server, so broadcast DHCP requests never reach 192.168.10.50 across the router.

symptom: No PC in VLAN 20 (192.168.20.0/24) can obtain a DHCP address, even though the pool shows 0 leases.
topology_note: DHCP pool DHCP-VLAN20 covers the full 192.168.20.0/24 range on R1.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.20.1 192.168.20.254
ip dhcp pool DHCP-VLAN20
 network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: The excluded-address range covers the entire VLAN 20 subnet (.1 to .254), leaving zero usable addresses in the pool.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 70 receive a valid IP address and subnet mask from DHCP but cannot reach any subnet outside VLAN 70.
topology_note: R1's actual gateway interface for VLAN 70 is 192.168.70.1; DHCP pool DHCP-VLAN70 is configured on R1.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config | section DHCP-VLAN70
ip dhcp pool DHCP-VLAN70
 network 192.168.70.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.70.254
 dns-server 192.168.70.5
expected_fault: The DHCP pool's default-router option is set to 192.168.70.254, which is not the router's real interface address (192.168.70.1), so clients get an unreachable gateway.
concept_tag: DHCP Option Misconfiguration - Wrong Default Gateway

symptom: PC can successfully ping Server1 at 192.168.10.5 but 'ping server1.netsage.local' fails with 'Ping request could not find host'.
topology_note: Internal DNS server 192.168.10.5 hosts zone netsage.local; PC obtained IP via DHCP.
show_outputs:
PC> ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: (none)
---
PC> ping server1.netsage.local
Ping request could not find host server1.netsage.local.
expected_fault: The PC has no DNS server address configured, so hostname resolution fails while direct IP connectivity works normally.

symptom: All PCs can ping the DNS server address they were given but every hostname lookup times out for internal and external names.
topology_note: DNS server is configured on host 192.168.10.5; PCs point to a DNS server address distributed via DHCP.
show_outputs:
PC> ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 192.168.10.50
---
PC> ping 192.168.10.50
Request timed out.
---
PC> ping 192.168.10.5
Reply from 192.168.10.5: bytes=32 time<1ms TTL=128
expected_fault: PCs are configured to use DNS server 192.168.10.50, which does not exist on the network, instead of the actual DNS server at 192.168.10.5.

symptom: Users can resolve 'server1.netsage.local' successfully but 'printer1.netsage.local' fails to resolve, even though both hosts are online.
topology_note: DNS server 192.168.10.5 hosts the netsage.local zone with A records for known hosts.
show_outputs: DNS-Server# show dns records netsage.local\nserver1.netsage.local  A  192.168.10.5\n(no entry for printer1.netsage.local)
expected_fault: The DNS zone is missing the A record for printer1.netsage.local, so only that specific host fails to resolve while others succeed.

symptom: Every PC on the network suddenly loses the ability to resolve any hostname, though IP connectivity to all hosts still works.
topology_note: DNS service runs on the dedicated Server1 (192.168.10.5).
show_outputs:
Server1> Services > DNS
DNS Service: Off
---
PC> ping 192.168.10.5
Reply from 192.168.10.5: bytes=32 time<1ms TTL=128
expected_fault: The DNS service on Server1 has been turned off, so it no longer answers any DNS queries network-wide.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/24) on R1 cannot reach hosts in VLAN 99 (192.168.99.0/24) on R2, though both routers are up and directly connected via a serial link.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip route
C 192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C 10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
(no route to 192.168.99.0/24)
expected_fault: R1 has no route (static or dynamic) to the 192.168.99.0/24 network, so traffic toward VLAN 99 is dropped at R1.

symptom: OSPF routes for VLAN 99 are missing from R1's routing table even though the serial link to R2 shows up/up.
topology_note: R1 and R2 are intended to run OSPF area 0 over the Se0/0/0 link (10.0.0.0/30).
show_outputs:
R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(empty)
---
R1# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
---
R2# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 1
expected_fault: R2's OSPF network statement uses area 1 while R1 uses area 0, so the OSPF adjacency never forms and routes are not exchanged.

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 10 cannot reach the 192.168.99.0/24 network; traceroute shows the packet leaving R1 but never returning.
topology_note: R1 has a static route configured toward 192.168.99.0/24 via the R1-R2 serial link 10.0.0.0/30 (valid host range .1-.2).
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config | include ip route
ip route 192.168.99.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.6
---
R1# show ip route
S 192.168.99.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.6
expected_fault: The static route's next-hop 10.0.0.6 is outside the point-to-point /30 subnet, so it points to an unreachable address and the route is effectively unusable.

symptom: All internal VLANs can reach each other normally, but no PC on the network can reach the internet (8.8.8.8).
topology_note: R1 connects to the ISP via Gi0/1 (203.0.113.2/30); internal routing between VLANs works through EIGRP.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip route
D 192.168.10.0/24
D 192.168.20.0/24
C 203.0.113.0/30 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
(no default route present)
expected_fault: R1 has no default route (ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0) toward the ISP, so traffic to any external destination is dropped.

symptom: PC1 can ping Server1 (192.168.10.5) successfully, but opening http://192.168.10.5 in the browser times out.
topology_note: Extended ACL 101 is applied inbound on R1 Gi0/0 to restrict traffic toward the server subnet.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
 10 permit icmp any 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
 20 deny tcp any 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 eq 80
 30 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL 101 explicitly denies TCP port 80 (HTTP) to the server subnet while permitting ICMP, so ping succeeds but web access is blocked.

symptom: Server1 in VLAN 10 stops responding to established client sessions from VLAN 20 right after a new security ACL was added on R1.
topology_note: ACL 110 was intended to filter traffic leaving VLAN 20 toward the server subnet, applied on R1 Gi0/0.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config interface gi0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip access-group 110 out
---
R1# show access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
 10 permit tcp 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 established
expected_fault: ACL 110 is applied outbound (out) on the interface facing the server subnet instead of inbound, so it filters the server's return traffic rather than the intended client-to-server traffic.

symptom: After applying a new ACL meant to restrict Telnet to R1, all traffic through Gi0/0 - including HTTP, ICMP, and DNS - stopped working.
topology_note: ACL 115 was intended to block only Telnet (TCP 23) inbound on R1 Gi0/0.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 115
Extended IP access list 115
 10 deny tcp any any eq 23
(no permit statements)
expected_fault: ACL 115 contains only a deny statement with no explicit permit, so the implicit 'deny ip any any' at the end blocks all other traffic in addition to Telnet.

symptom: Host 192.168.20.15 was supposed to be specifically blocked from reaching Server1, but it can still connect fine while the rest of VLAN 20 is blocked as intended.
topology_note: ACL 120 applied inbound on R1 Gi1/0, intended to deny 192.168.20.15 specifically and permit the rest of VLAN 20.
expected_fault: The broad permit statement for the whole 192.168.20.0/24 subnet is listed before the specific deny for 192.168.20.15, so the host matches the permit first and the deny is never reached.

symptom: Internal PCs (192.168.10.0/24) can ping R1's own interfaces and reach other internal subnets, but cannot reach any internet address such as 8.8.8.8.
topology_note: R1 Gi0/1 connects to the ISP (203.0.113.2/30); NAT overload is intended for internal-to-internet translation.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config | include ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip nat inside
(no ip nat outside on any interface)
expected_fault: No interface is marked 'ip nat outside', so NAT never triggers on outbound traffic and internal addresses are sent untranslated onto the internet, where they are dropped.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/24) reach the internet fine, but PCs in the newly added VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24) cannot.
topology_note: R1 performs NAT overload referencing access-list 1 for permitted inside sources.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 1
Standard IP access list 1
 10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
---
R1# show ip nat translations
(only 192.168.10.x entries present)
expected_fault: Access-list 1, which defines which inside networks get NAT-translated, only permits 192.168.10.0/24 and does not include 192.168.30.0/24, so VLAN 30 traffic is never translated.

symptom: External users trying to reach the published web server at 203.0.113.10 cannot connect, though the server itself has full internet access outbound.
topology_note: Static NAT is supposed to map public IP 203.0.113.10 to Server1's internal address 192.168.10.5.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config | include ip nat inside source static
ip nat inside source static 192.168.10.50 203.0.113.10
---
Server1 actual IP: 192.168.10.5
expected_fault: The static NAT entry maps 203.0.113.10 to 192.168.10.50 instead of Server1's real address 192.168.10.5, so inbound connections are forwarded to the wrong host.

symptom: Laptop attempting to join 'NetSage-WiFi' repeatedly prompts for the password and fails to associate, though signal strength is full.
topology_note: Wireless AP1 broadcasts SSID 'NetSage-WiFi' secured with WPA2-PSK.
show_outputs:
AP1# show running-config | include wpa
authentication key-management wpa
wpa-psk ascii 0 NetSage2024!
---
Laptop saved profile passphrase: NetSage2023!
expected_fault: The laptop's saved wireless profile uses passphrase 'NetSage2023!' while the AP is configured with 'NetSage2024!', so WPA2-PSK authentication fails.

symptom: Wireless laptops associate to the AP and receive an IP address, but cannot ping or reach any wired PC in VLAN 10, even though wired PCs in VLAN 10 reach each other fine.
topology_note: AP1's uplink switch port SW1 Fa0/10 should map the WLAN to VLAN 10; wired PCs are also in VLAN 10.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces fa0/10 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 99 (default)
---
Wireless client IP: 192.168.99.20/24 (from VLAN 99 DHCP scope)
expected_fault: The AP's uplink port Fa0/10 is assigned to VLAN 99 instead of VLAN 10, placing all wireless clients in the wrong VLAN and subnet, isolated from the wired VLAN 10 devices.

symptom: Wireless clients successfully associate and authenticate to the AP but never receive an IP address, staying on a self-assigned 169.254.x.x address.
topology_note: AP1 uplink to SW1 Gi0/1 is a trunk carrying VLAN 10 (wired) and VLAN 40 (wireless); DHCP for VLAN 40 is served by R1.
show_outputs: SW1# show interfaces gi0/1 trunk\nVlans allowed on trunk: 1,10\n(VLAN 40 not listed)
expected_fault: VLAN 40 (the wireless VLAN) is not included in the allowed VLAN list on the AP's uplink trunk, so wireless client DHCP broadcasts never reach the switch/router and no address is assigned.
concept_tag: Wireless VLAN Pruned from Uplink Trunk
